in_hebrew.name: ניקולאו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ניקולאו הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית, ומשמעותו 'נוער לנצח' או 'כובש העם'. השם ניקולאו הוא גרסה עברית של השם היווני Νικόλαος, שמורכב מהמילים 'נίκη' (ניצחון) ו'לאוס' (עם). השם ניקולאו היה נפוץ בקרב הנוצרים בימי הביניים, והוא קשור לקדוש ניקולאי, קדוש נוצרי חשוב.

in_greek.name: Νικολάου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Νικολάου προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'νίκη' (νίκη) και 'λαός' (λαός), που σημαίνει 'νίκη του λαού' ή 'αυτός που κατακτά τον λαό'. Το όνομα ήταν πολύ δημοφιλές στην αρχαία Ελλάδα και συνδέεται με τον Άγιο Νικόλαο, έναν από τους πιο δημοφιλείς αγίους της Ανατολικής Ορθόδοξης Εκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Nicolau
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Nicolau derivatur ex Graecis verbis 'nike' (victoria) et 'laos' (populus), quod significat 'victor populi' vel 'is qui populum obtinet'. Nomen hoc erat usitatum inter Christianos in medio aevo, et coniungitur cum Sancto Nicolao, sancto patrono importante.

in_english.name: Nicolau
in_english.meaning: Nicolau - victor of the people, conquering the nation
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nicolau originates from the Greek words 'nike' (victory) and 'laos' (people), meaning 'victor of the people' or 'conquering the nation'. Nicolau is a variant of the name Nicholas, which was popularized by Saint Nicholas, a 4th-century bishop of Myra (modern-day Turkey). The name has been used across various Christian cultures, symbolizing spiritual victory and leadership.

saint_reference.note: Bishop of Myra, known for generosity and kindness

data.cultural_impact: The name Nicolau is a common name in various Christian cultures, particularly in Europe, due to the influence of Saint Nicholas, who was known for his generosity and gift-giving during the holiday season. Over time, Saint Nicholas evolved into Santa Claus in the Western world, sharing the same connotation of gift-giving and joy. Thus, the name Nicolau carries a rich cultural heritage connected to the celebration of generosity and love.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nicolau holds significant spiritual meaning in the Christian faith, as it was borne by many early saints and martyrs. It is a reminder of the belief in the power of the community in overcoming adversity, encapsulated in the etymology of the name - victory of the people. The name carries a sense of hope, strength, and courage, inspiring those who bear it to remain steadfast in their faith and to offer compassion and support to those around them. Additionally, the various patronages associated with Saint Nicholas underscore the spiritual importance of elements of Christian life, such as faith, hope, charity, and generosity.
